falsification_F1_to_F5.F-1_SET_IDENTITY: FIRES at any named cell and arm where the MEASURED misalignment set is not EQUAL, AS A SET, to the PREDICTED set for that arm - which is the empty set or T(cell) for arm A-prime (P-1, P-2) and MIS(A-prime, cell) for arm E-prime (P-3, the only set prediction this contract makes for that arm; so for arm E-prime F-1 and F-4 coincide by construction, and that is stated rather than left to be noticed). A CARDINALITY MATCH WITH A DIFFERENT MEMBER SET FIRES F-1 and is recorded as `cardinality_only_agreement`. The report NAMES THE CELLS and gives the symmetric difference.
falsification_F1_to_F5.F-2_STATIC_BOUND: FIRES at any named cell and arm where alpha > |MIS|. CELLS NAMED. A firing contradicts Corollary 2b of the derivation note, which is exact linear algebra over the field F_n, so it indicates an implementation defect in `matrix_rank_mod` or in the driver's MIS computation. IT IS REPORTED AS SUCH AND IT DOES NOT INVALIDATE THE RUN: a criterion may not delete the evidence that fired it.
falsification_F1_to_F5.F-3_LADDER: FIRES if and only if the set of ladder cells at which alpha(A-prime) = 0 is not EQUAL to the L0 set {L12, L24, L48, L96, L192}. The report names the members of the symmetric difference. THIS IS THE INDEPENDENCE-OF-B FALSIFIER FOR ARM A-PRIME and it is stated as a set identity over NAMED cells, never as "alpha did not grow".
falsification_F1_to_F5.F-4_DIAGNOSTICITY: FIRES if and only if the set of named cells at which alpha(E-prime) = alpha(A-prime) is not EQUAL to the full fourteen-cell set. The report names the members of the symmetric difference AND, for each, states THE DIRECTION of the inequality. F-4 FIRING IS NOT A FAILURE OF THE EXPERIMENT: it is the outcome under which the phi-invariant factor base is doing something, and it is the outcome this program has been unable to obtain cleanly for three batches. See interpretation_limits for what a firing does and does not license.
falsification_F1_to_F5.F-5_B_INDEPENDENCE_OF_THE_BOUND: FIRES, PER ARM, if and only if the set of the ten ladder cells at which alpha <= 3 is not EQUAL to the full ten-cell ladder set {L12, L13, L24, L25, L48, L49, L96, L97, L192, L193}. CELLS NAMED. This is the direct test of H-STR-002's own words - "alpha <= r = 3 for phi-invariant factor bases at all tested B" - at a FIXED curve over a sixteen-fold range of B.

verdict_rule: THE EXECUTOR COMPUTES AND RECORDS EXACTLY ONE VERDICT IN results/sweep_summary.json AND INTERPRETS NONE OF THEM. `instrument_artifact_confirmed` - F-1 fires at no cell for either arm AND F-4 does not fire. `instrument_artifact_falsified` - F-1 does not fire for arm A-prime AND the set of cells at which alpha(E-prime) > alpha(A-prime) is NON-EMPTY and is NAMED. `mixed` - the named cells point different ways: the agreement set of F-4 is a non-empty PROPER subset of the fourteen. `incomplete` - any named cell was not measured, any stopping rule fired, any certificate failed, or a base-row shortfall excluded a cell from the comparative criteria. UNDER `mixed` OR `incomplete` THE COORDINATOR'S DECISION ON THE INSTRUMENT QUESTION IS `inconclusive`, AND SAYING SO PLAINLY IS THE REQUIRED OUTCOME. The F-3 and F-5 ladder verdicts are recorded as SEPARATE fields (`ladder_verdict_F3`, `ladder_verdict_F5_A_prime`, `ladder_verdict_F5_E_prime`) and are NEVER folded into the instrument verdict. No criterion may be changed after any outcome is observed without a versioned protocol_amendment under experiments/EXP-STR-004/amendments/; an outcome-driven revision is exploratory and cannot be evaluated against this confirmatory criterion.
